subject.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage

question: Should the project adopt this five-stage localization contract as the v1 direction, and which owner-approved foundation decisions may proceed before Gateway, channel, plugin-metadata, and release-gate work?
rationale: The RFC explicitly requests decisions from several product owners and proposes new cross-surface contracts; implementation quality cannot determine whether those permanent API and release-policy boundaries are desired.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow v1 foundation
options.body: Approve only locale resolution, reviewed English fallback, and internal message descriptors first, while deferring wire, plugin, and release-contract decisions to their owners.

options.title: Request an owner-scoped RFC revision
options.body: Keep the RFC draft and ask it to name decision owners, compatibility commitments, and acceptance criteria for each later workstream before sponsorship.

options.title: Defer the program
options.body: Leave existing surface-specific localization paths in place until the project has capacity to own the required cross-product contracts.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow v1 foundation
recommendation.body: Approve only locale resolution, reviewed English fallback, and internal message descriptors first, while deferring wire, plugin, and release-contract decisions to their owners.

likelyOwner.reason: The author is the only evidence-backed routing contact in the supplied context; a project owner must ultimately sponsor the product decision.
